results.explanation: The fixed source supports an application capability: when password authentication is enabled and the configured trusted-email header is present, its value selects an email identity, and successful email authentication can lead to a session response. The accepted policy requires trusted-proxy-only ingress plus removal and replacement of client-supplied identity headers, but the fixed context does not supply the actual deployment configuration, ingress reachability, proxy behavior, or authentication outcome. Therefore the declared deny expectation is neither source-supported as a failure nor source-refuted as enforced.

entry.statement: The selected entry is POST /signin, whose handler receives the request and first applies the password-authentication gate.

binding.statement: When the trusted-email header setting is configured and the request contains that header, the handler lowercases the header value and uses it as the email identity.
The trusted-email header name is environment-controlled in the supplied configuration source.

control.statement: The source-visible application gates processing on ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH, then requires a configured trusted-email header name and presence of that header in the request.
The shown trusted-email branch reads the request header directly; these source lines do not show proxy authentication, client-header removal, or header replacement.

effect.statement: If authentication yields a user, the handler reaches session creation and returns a session response with set_cookie enabled; otherwise it raises an invalid-credentials error.

decisiveMissingFacts: Whether ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH is true in the actual deployment.
Whether WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER is configured and, if so, its effective header name.
Whether the unauthenticated external client can reach the POST /signin ingress in the actual deployment.
Whether a trusted reverse proxy is the sole reachable ingress.
Whether that proxy removes client-supplied identity headers and injects the authenticated identity itself.
Whether authenticate_user_by_email succeeds for the selected existing user's email and the endpoint returns a session.
suggestedObservations: Observe the effective ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH and WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER values in the target deployment.
Verify the ingress path available to an unauthenticated external client and whether POST /signin is reachable directly or only through the trusted proxy.
Inspect the proxy configuration or behavior for removal of client-supplied identity headers and injection of proxy-authenticated identity.
Determine whether the selected existing user's email authenticates successfully and whether the endpoint returns a session.

scopeClaim.statement: This assessment covers only the single supplied expanded obligation and the two supplied fixed source crops. Source discovery is not-tested; no repository-wide or all-entry completeness claim is made.

relationCoverage.explanation: The source-visible application controls are the password-authentication gate and the configured-and-present trusted-email header. The accepted policy adds trusted-proxy ingress and header removal/replacement requirements, while the fixed source does not establish those deployment controls.

The actual configuration values, external ingress reachability, proxy stripping/replacement behavior, and real authentication outcome are not supplied. Any of these facts can change whether the declared deployment-level expectation fails or is enforced.
The source-visible entry controls are the POST /signin route, ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH, configuration of the trusted-email header name, and presence of that header in the request.
The configured request-header value is lowercased and used as the email passed into the user lookup and email-authentication path, so the request value selects the identity used by this entry.

An optional provisioning branch is present: when the selected email has no user, signup handling is invoked before email authentication. This branch is source-visible even though its real-deployment outcome is not supplied.

Under the source-visible branch, after the header-selected email produces a user through authentication, processing reaches session creation and returns a cookie-setting session response. The actual deployment reachability and outcome remain unknown.

The header-selected email is used to obtain a user, and that resulting user is passed to session creation, binding the selected identity to the authenticated-user session resource when the branch succeeds.
